newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends softer as banks shift to dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends softer as banks shift to dlrs.

text.p: * Falling overnight peso rate triggers dollar buying
The Philippine peso softened to 26.297 to the dollar at close against 26.283 as banks shifted to the U.S. currency after local interest rates eased, traders said.
"After selling their dollars yesterday, banks were left with excess pesos and low interest rates," one trader said. The situation prompted banks to shift portfolios back to dollar holdings.

The peso had strengthened on Wednesday as banks sold dollars to finance their peso reserve deficiencies. With the overnight peso rate rising to a high of 12.75 percent, banks had sold over $268 million.
But on Thursday, overnight money slipped to 11.0625 percent on ample liquidity.
Another trader viewed today's dollar-buying as mere short-covering. "Some sold more than what they needed," one trader said.
The peso was hovering between 26.288 to 26.290 for deals to be settled tomorrow. Some banks bought dollars at 26.297 for value Monday on small volume.
A total of $109 million was traded on Thursday.
The Central Bank posted its selling price at 26.292 and buying rate at 26.252.
Traders expected the peso to drift sideways with no significant flow either way to influence the rate.
